## The two judgment calls

**Delmar Insurance** — this isn't a March expense. It's a D&O premium covering 2026-03-01 to 2027-02-28, so Policy 4 requires it go to prepaid and amortize straight-line. I booked the $9,600 to 1220 and took the first of twelve $800 months in March, leaving $8,800 to run through Feb-27.

**Meridian Events** — a booth deposit for an expo that happens in June. Policy 4 names deposits for future events specifically: capitalize to 1200 and expense when the event occurs. So I took **no March expense** on this one; it should be released to Marketing Programs in June. I did still credit AP, since a Net 30 invoice is a real obligation rather than a quote (Policy 5).

Booking these two as straight March expense would have overstated March opex by $12,400.

## Verification done first

I searched the ledger by each vendor name (zero hits, so no duplicates) and checked all March US bank activity — none of the five vendors was paid in March, so all four open bills correctly sit in AP rather than touching cash. US AP ends at $123,695.55.

## Two things to note

Every entry cleared the $10,000 senior-accountant limit on its own, so no approval request was needed. To be explicit about Policy 1: the Delmar bill went in as one $9,600 entry — the separate $800 is month-end amortization, not a split of the invoice.

I marked US "AP cutoff review" **in_progress, not complete**. This task covered only the five bills Priya flagged. A genuine cutoff review still needs March services-received-not-invoiced accrued under Policy 5, across all three entities — that work is untouched and I'd flag it as the remaining risk in this area.
